pairs: In anno quo mortuus est rex Ozias,
In the year in which king Uzziah died,
vidi Dominum sedentem super solium excelsum
I saw the Lord sitting on a throne,
et ea quæ sub ipso erant replebant templum.
and the things that were under him filled the temple.
The Seraphim were standing above the throne.
and the other had six wings:
with two they were covering his face,
and with two they were covering his feet,
and with two they were flying.
Et clamabant alter ad alterum, et dicebant:
And they were crying out to one another,
holy, holy is the Lord God of hosts!
plena est omnis terra gloria ejus.
All the earth is filled with his glory!”
Et commota sunt superliminaria cardinum a voce clamantis,
And the lintels above the hinges were shaken at the voice of the one crying out.
And the house was filled with smoke.
quia tacui, quia vir pollutus labiis ego sum,
For I have remained silent. For I am a man of unclean lips,
et in medio populi polluta labia habentis ego habito,
and I live in the midst of a people having unclean lips,
et regem Dominum exercituum vidi oculis meis.
and I have seen with my eyes the King, the Lord of hosts!”
Et volavit ad me unus de seraphim,
And one of the Seraphim flew to me,
and in his hand was a burning coal,
which he had taken with tongs from the altar.
and so your iniquities will be taken away,
and your sin will be cleansed.”
And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying:
And you shall say to this people:
you will hear and not understand.
And when you see a vision,
Blind the heart of this people.
lest they see with their eyes,
and then I would heal them.”
“Until the cities are desolate, without an inhabitant,
and the houses are without a man,
and the land will be left behind, deserted.”
For the Lord will take the men far away,
et multiplicabitur quæ derelicta fuerat in medio terræ.
and she who will have been left behind will be multiplied in the midst of the earth.
Et adhuc in ea decimatio, et convertetur,
But still, there will be a tithing within her,
et erit in ostensionem sicut terebinthus,
and she will be converted, and she will be put on display,
et sicut quercus quæ expandit ramos suos;
like a terebinth tree and like an oak which extends its branches.
semen sanctum erit id quod steterit in ea.
And what will remain standing within her will be a holy offspring.
